notes.text: Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Matt Coronato has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee.
Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 11 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 10 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Maxim Tsyplakov returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ben Jones was added to the roster on Oct 21 and has played beside Joel Farabee and Matt Coronato.

COL.head: A big edge for the Avalanche
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Calgary is on the second night of a back-to-back. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with keeping dangerous shots away.

CGY.head: The Avalanche should be favored
CGY.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Calgary is on the second night of a back-to-back. To pull this off, the Flames can start with keeping dangerous shots away, plus Dustin Wolf stealing the show.

story.head: Fresh legs vs. Tired ones
paras: The Avalanche won the teams’ first meeting this season, 7-3 in Calgary on Oct 8. The Flames (6-7-0) beat Seattle 6-2 last night, and the Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 on Wednesday. Going in, the Flames are fifth in the Pacific (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 16th).

Both teams play fast, open games and do a lot of their shooting from distance. The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). As for the Avalanche, they get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.15 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames, and good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Flames.

Joel Farabee (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (5 G / 5 A / 10 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals, with seven points in his last five games. Nathan MacKinnon (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 13 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL, with a point in five straight games against Calgary. Artturi Lehkonen (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 13 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games.

Dustin Wolf (2-4-0 / .848 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start. Colorado has two options in net: Mackenzie Blackwood (6-3-0 / .894 SV% in 9 GS) and Scott Wedgewood (1-2-1 / .889 SV% in 4 GS). Blackwood has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Blackwood has a .939 save percentage in five starts against the Flames, well above his usual .905. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.

items.text: The Flames are newly without Devin Cooley, have been without Samuel Honzek, Joel Hanley and Connor Zary for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season. Dustin Wolf is expected to start.
Artturi Lehkonen has ten goals on chances worth about 4.4 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Zachary L'Heureux and Matt Coronato fought the last time these two met.
